title: Choose Bork's visual world
question: Bork can leave Twitter behind. Choose the world that should make the feed memorable without making it harder to use.

options.label: Kennel Run Ledger
options.lineage: boarding kennel run cards and working shift boards
options.thesis: A living pack ledger where every bork reads like a fresh entry on a well-run kennel board.
options.viewport: A compact utility rail frames one broad feed sheet; the composer is the active run card and the newest borks stack below with clear status marks.
options.risk: The operational language can feel clinical if warm dog portraits and humane copy do not lead.

raised.raise: Posting gets one deliberate develop-and-settle transition instead of scattered animation.
Scale, not extra chrome, identifies the active author, new activity, and secondary metadata.
The layout changes only in whole functional units so mobile never receives a crushed desktop board.
One directional pack-trail motion links composing to the new feed entry.

options.label: Trailhead Pack Map
options.lineage: municipal park wayfinding and trail-condition boards
options.thesis: The feed is the trailhead where the pack checks in, leaves a mark, and follows familiar names into the park.
options.viewport: A bold trailhead masthead hands directly into a readable route-like feed, with the compose action fixed as the unmistakable orange trail marker.
options.risk: Park wayfinding is familiar enough that timid execution could read like outdoors-brand marketing.

options.label: Bork OS
options.thesis: A crisp black-and-white desktop turns profiles, posts, and settings into direct little tools for the pack.
options.viewport: The timeline owns the primary window while a small pack navigator and composer overlap it with strict, legible hierarchy.
options.case: Developer recognition is immediate and the window model maps cleanly to the app, but the dog audience arrives through content rather than the world itself.
options.risk: Retro novelty wins if dither, type scale, or window behavior become decoration instead of structure.

options.label: Fetch Console
options.thesis: Bork becomes a tactile social console whose single orange key makes publishing feel obvious and satisfying.
options.viewport: A disciplined control rail surrounds one amber live-feed screen; the orange BORK key is the only loud action.
options.case: It identifies strongly with developers and clarifies actions through tactile state, but it carries less innate dog-world recognition than the kennel ledger.
options.risk: Literal knobs and keys could turn a simple social feed into a dashboard cosplay.

options.label: Safelight Developing Bay
options.lineage: a printing darkroom under amber safelight
options.thesis: New borks slowly emerge like wet prints moving through a deliberate publishing process.
options.viewport: A linear compose-to-develop station precedes a drying-line feed of finished posts.
options.case: The publishing metaphor is strong, but dog lovers do not identify with the setting and routine reading becomes unnecessarily ceremonial.
options.kept: One continuous reveal should make a completed post feel real.
options.risk: The atmosphere can overpower a routine feed action.

options.label: Pack Star Atlas
options.thesis: People and borks become a navigable constellation of the pack.
options.viewport: A plotted pack map dominates while the readable post stream sits in a chart index.
options.case: It is memorable, but mapping relationships that Bork does not actually model would promise a richer network than exists.
options.kept: Importance should be legible through a disciplined magnitude scale.
options.risk: The chart implies social graph features the project does not have.

options.label: Deployable Feed Sheet
options.thesis: The compact feed unfolds into linked authors, posts, and details without losing its crease logic.
options.viewport: A tessellated post field expands from the active composer cell.
options.case: Its responsive system is rigorous, but the fold metaphor adds navigation work without helping visitors understand Bork.
options.kept: Responsive changes should preserve complete functional units.
options.risk: Clever geometry could obscure ordinary reading order.

options.label: Gravity Dog Park
options.thesis: Borks travel through a surreal park along visible directional scent trails.
options.viewport: One gravity field carries the newest bork into a grounded reading lane.
options.case: The signature motion is delightful, but the world weakens product clarity and asks too much performance from a resume project.
options.kept: One directional motion can connect cause and result without animating everything.
options.risk: The simulation would become the product instead of supporting it.

canonCard.label: Polished social feed
canonCard.thesis: The familiar three-column Twitter-clone arrangement, executed with excellent spacing, states, and dog-themed copy.
canonCard.viewport: Navigation, centered timeline, and secondary rail follow the social-product layout visitors already know.
canonCard.risk: It is easiest to understand and hardest to remember.
